title: Constant-coefficient finiteness for projective smooth curves
statement:
Let $S$ be Noetherian
and let $f:X\to S$ be
projective and
smooth, with geometric fibres
of pure dimension one. If $\ell$ is a prime invertible on $S$,
every higher direct image
$R^rf_*\mathbf F_\ell$ is
constructible.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], the projective morphism $f$ is proper. Set $F=\mathbf F_\ell$, the constant sheaf on $X$: it is a finite module sheaf over the finite coefficient ring $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$.

Apply [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] to $f$, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and $F$. For every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$ and every $r\geq0$ it identifies the geometric stalk $(R^rf_*F)_{\bar s}$ with $H^r(X_{\bar s},F|_{X_{\bar s}})$. The restriction of a constant sheaf is constant, so the latter group is $H^r(X_{\bar s},\mathbf F_\ell)$.

By [lem-fin-projective-curve-betti-cardinalities], these fibre cohomology groups are finite and their cardinality functions have constructible level sets. The lemma applies because $S$ is Noetherian, $f$ is smooth and projective with geometric fibres of pure dimension one, and $\ell$ is a prime invertible on $S$.

Fix $r\geq0$. By definition, $R^rf_*F$ is an abelian etale sheaf on the Noetherian scheme $S$. Its geometric stalks are finite, and for every integer $n\geq1$ the level set $C_n=\{s\in S:|(R^rf_*F)_{\bar s}|=n\}$ is constructible: the stalk isomorphisms of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] identify it with the corresponding cardinality locus of [lem-fin-projective-curve-betti-cardinalities]. Thus [fin4-lem-stalk-constructibility-criterion] gives a finite locally closed partition on which this sheaf is finite locally constant. This also gives constructibility as an $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf: scalar multiplication by a class modulo $\ell$ is repeated addition, so every additive trivialization is $\mathbf F_\ell$-linear. Since $r$ was arbitrary, every higher direct image is constructible.
